metadata.methods_description: EEG recordings were obtained from 20 healthy, right-handed participants (mean age 24.55 ± 2.58 years; 11 female, 9 male) during three speech conditions: overt speech, silent articulation, and imagined speech. Participants viewed Pinyin stimuli on a screen and performed the corresponding speech task. The stimulus set comprised 6 initials (m, f, j, l, k, ch) and 4 finals (a, i, u, ü). Each participant completed 4 blocks totaling 1600 trials.

citation_details.title: 3M-CPSEED, An EEG-based Dataset for Chinese Pinyin Production in Overt, Mouthed, and Imagined Speech
citation_details.author: Xiuying Ma, Yi Jiang, Ning Jiang
citation_details.abstract: Speech brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) enable communication with the external world by decoding neural signals. However, language function as a higher-order brain function, the neural mechanisms underlying speech production remain incompletely understood. Currently most existing Chinese EEG datasets use sentences as stimuli, overlooking that Pinyin constitutes the phonetic foundation of Chinese characters, which limits research on decoding individual Chinese character components. Moreover, most datasets employ only one speech production paradigm, preventing exploration of the brain's diverse speech production modes. This study aims to construct the 3M-CPSEED Chinese Pinyin dataset for exploring neural activity during three distinct speech modes (overt speech, silently articulated speech, imagined speech)of syllables from distinct articulatory positions. The dataset comprises EEG recordings from 20 participants completing four experimental blocks within one day, yielding 1,800 validated trials. 3M-CPSEED holds significant implications for speech neurophysiology research, not only facilitating exploration of neural activity differences across pinyin articulations but also enabling robust transfer learning studies for other alphabetic languages.

citation_details.title: 3M-CPSEED：An EEG-based Dataset for Chinese Pinyin Production in Overt, Silent-intended, and Imagined Speech
citation_details.author: Xinyu Ma, Jiang Yi, Ning Jiang
citation_details.abstract: 3M-CPSEED is an EEG dataset comprising recordings from 20 native Chinese speakers performing overt, silently articulated, and imagined speech tasks using Chinese Pinyin phonemes. The dataset captures neural activity across 6 initials (m, f, j, l, k, ch) and 4 finals (a, i, u, ü), with 1600 trials per participant. This resource supports investigation of neural mechanisms underlying speech production and enables transfer learning applications for alphabetic language research. The dataset is a BIDS-formatted re-hosting of OpenNeuro dataset ds006465 (version 2.0.0) on NEMAR.
